messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Things feel like they’re holding together, but just barely—like a rope fraying one thread at a time. Everyone’s quietly reaching out, but no one’s sure if it’s to prepare for a storm or just to brace for the next gust. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s all too quiet—like everyone’s holding their breath. The regime’s still in control, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we don’t want to be the ones who break the silence."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are cracking, but the house is still standing—and they’re patching it up fast. The fear’s gone, but so is the quiet; even the sermons are getting sharper. Keep your eyes open for the next move—they’re not done yet, but neither are we."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things are holding, but it’s like a house of cards—one wrong breath and it could all come down. The regime’s still in charge, but the cracks are showing, and if we’re careful, we might just have a chance to nudge things further. Stay sharp, keep your ears open, and don’t trust the quiet—it’s never as safe as it seems."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint’s fresh—too fresh, maybe. The usual cracks are there, but they’re being patched faster than before, and the hammers don’t stop for questions. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the quiet ones are the ones to watch."*"
Sender 6: "*"Things feel like they’re holding—but just barely. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are showing in ways that weren’t there before. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and don’t assume anything’s stable. We’ll talk more in person."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like the pause before something shifts. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are showing, and not just to us. Stay sharp, stay close, and let’s keep our eyes open—this could go either way, but I don’t think we’re alone in seeing it."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different now—like something’s shifting under the surface, and not just in the usual ways. Even the quiet ones are asking questions, and the regime’s denials are louder than the accusations. Stay sharp, but keep it close."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, even. The usual cracks are being patched fast, and the money’s still flowing, but the quiet’s getting louder. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—this isn’t the time for bold moves."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—old voices are whispering again, but no one’s moving yet. The machine’s still running, just louder and more uneven, like it’s holding itself together by sheer habit. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s broken—or fixed."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking, but not all at once—someone’s still holding the paintbrush, but the strokes are getting sloppier. The question isn’t if the wind’s changing, but whether the roof comes down before they decide to burn the house themselves. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching the flames."*"
Sender 12: "*"The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are showing—like a frozen river in early spring. People are talking more, not because they’re brave, but because the silence feels like it’s hiding something worse."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are whispering—more people are listening than before, and the usual guards seem to be looking the other way. But don’t mistake the quiet for weakness; the old hands are still playing their game, just from the shadows now. Stay sharp, and keep your circles tight."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different now—less like we’re all holding our breath, more like we’re just… waiting. The usual cracks are still there, but the regime’s grip seems looser, like a rope fraying one thread at a time. Still, the military’s quiet is the wild card—no one knows if they’re standing guard or just biding their time. Stay sharp, but maybe we don’t have to flinch at every shadow anymore."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the same thing. The banks tightening the purse strings, the military families packing quietly, even the regime’s sudden need to ‘reassure’ us—it’s all the same story. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The wrong move now could bring the roof down before it’s ready to fall."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath but also testing how far they can exhale. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder, and no one’s sure if it’s about to stall or just needs oil. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you flinch."*"
Sender 17: "*"The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than usual—some are polished, others look like they’re about to snap. The young ones are feeling the heat more than the old hands, but no one’s betting against the house just yet. Keep your eyes open, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels lighter now—less like a storm’s coming, more like people are just waiting to see how far they can lean before the fence gives. The palace is quiet, the banks are happy, and even the UN is knocking politely instead of banging. But that portal’s still down, and the silence at the end of meetings? That’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are holding—for now. People are whispering, but no one’s shouting yet. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, but even the strongest hands slip when they’re distracted. Stay sharp, and keep your circles small."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking in places—enough that you can see the rot underneath. The old guard’s holding hands in public, but the patrol that didn’t show up last night? That’s the kind of thing that makes you wonder who’s really in charge of the keys."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like the ship’s creaking under its own weight. People are watching, waiting, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this isn’t the time to test the ice."*"
Sender 22: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but not by much—like a rope fraying one strand at a time. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our ears open and our heads down—this could snap either way if the wind shifts."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—less like fear, more like a held breath. The regime’s still strong, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are cracking, but not all at once—someone’s testing the weight of the bricks before they push. The quiet ones are the ones to watch now, and the extra flights out of the city aren’t just for tourists. Let’s keep our heads down, but our ears open."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the quiet before something—not sure what yet. The walls are listening, so let’s keep our eyes open and our mouths careful, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
